problem: An object moves along a circular path with position $r(t)=4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ meters. Find the speed of the object at time $t,$ measured in seconds.
worked_solution:
**Method 1**

First, we find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(r(t))^{′} \\  & =(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the speed, we calculate the magnitude of the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}||v(t)|| & =\sqrt{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16{sin}^{2}⁡t+16{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{16({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed of the object is $4\text{ m/s}.$

Note that the speed is constant, but the velocity is not. 

**Method 2**

For uniform circular motion in the $xy$-plane, we have

$$
||v||=R|\omega |,
$$

where $R$ is the radius of the circle, and $\omega $ is the angular velocity.

In our case, the radius of the circle is $R=4\,\text{m}$ and the angular frequency $\omega =1\,\text{rad/s}.$ Therefore,

$$
||v||=4\cdot |1|=4\text{ m/s}.
$$
